outline.title: The Inoculator
outline.premise: In the ruins of Manhattan, a plague doctor named Sable Voss moves through quarantine zones administering what she believes are life-saving inoculations to the dwindling survivor population. When she discovers that the pathogen decimating the city was engineered — and that her own syringes may be delivering a second, slower poison — she must confront the architects of the plague: a shadow collective called the Covenant who believe controlled die-off is the only path to civilizational rebirth. To save the survivors, Sable must bargain with the people who built the disease, and reckon with how deeply she has already served their agenda.
themes: Complicity and the danger of unexamined obedience
Trust as both survival tool and vulnerability
The moral cost of survival — what we become to endure
Manufactured hope as a weapon of control

characters.name: Sable Voss
characters.role: Protagonist — plague doctor and field inoculator
characters.arc: Begins as a dutiful healer who trusts her orders, and ends as a woman who must weaponize the Covenant's own cure against them, accepting that her hands were never clean.

characters.name: Dren Achebe
characters.role: Survivor and Sable's reluctant guide through the outer boroughs
characters.arc: Starts as a cynical scavenger who trusts no one, and dies protecting Sable after she earns the one thing he stopped believing in — someone worth trusting.

characters.name: Director Maren Solís
characters.role: Leader of the Covenant and Sable's former mentor
characters.arc: Revealed as the architect of the plague, she offers Sable the cure as a partnership, and is destroyed — not by violence but by Sable's public exposure of her design.

characters.name: The Covenant
characters.role: Shadow collective of scientists and former government officials
characters.arc: Function as a monolithic antagonist whose internal logic is chillingly coherent, collapsing when their secrecy is stripped away.

chapters.title: The Round
chapters.beat: Sable completes her daily inoculation route through a quarantine zone in lower Manhattan, moving among the sick with practiced efficiency, believing she is the last line between the survivors and extinction.
chapters.arc_notes: Exposition — establishes the ruined world, Sable's role and identity as healer, her trust in her orders, and the texture of daily survival; plants unease when a child she inoculated yesterday is found dead with no plague symptoms.

chapters.title: What the Vials Know
chapters.beat: Dren, a scavenger who has been tracking Sable's route, forces her at knifepoint into a basement lab where a dead biochemist's notes reveal that the pathogen has a synthetic marker — it was designed, not evolved — and that the inoculation serum contains a secondary compound with no medical justification.
chapters.arc_notes: Rising Action — escalates stakes by shattering Sable's foundational belief in her mission; the discovery of the synthetic marker tightens her options and forces an alliance with Dren; every assumption she has built her survival on is now suspect.

chapters.title: The Covenant's Offer
chapters.beat: Sable infiltrates the Covenant's fortified medical tower and confronts Director Solís, who confirms everything — the plague is engineered, the inoculations are a population-management tool — and offers Sable a place at the table, presenting the true cure as proof of good faith and framing mass die-off as necessary mathematics.
chapters.arc_notes: Climax — the apex of Freytag's Pyramid; Sable reaches the truth she sought and is offered complicity as its price; she takes the cure from Solís's hand, and in doing so crosses a threshold — she now holds the power to save or to continue serving the Covenant's design; the first crack appears when she sees Dren has been captured outside.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Vial
chapters.beat: Sable escapes with the cure formula but cannot save Dren before Covenant soldiers kill him; alone in the ruins, she synthesizes doses from the dead biochemist's lab and begins distributing the true cure — but each survivor she saves is a person the Covenant will now mark as a loose end, and she knows she has started a war she cannot finish.
chapters.arc_notes: Falling Action — consequence of the climax ripples outward; Dren's death makes the moral weight of Sable's choice irreversible and personal; her act of distribution is simultaneously heroic and a death sentence for those she saves; transformation is made visible — she is no longer a healer following orders but a woman who has chosen her own complicity and is now trying to undo it.

chapters.title: Inoculation
chapters.beat: Sable broadcasts the Covenant's full design — the engineered plague, the false inoculations, Solís's identity — over every surviving radio frequency in the city, then walks back into the quarantine zones with the last of the true cure, knowing the Covenant will come for her and that the exposure is the only medicine that cannot be recalled.
chapters.arc_notes: Resolution — closes the dramatic question of whether Sable will serve the system or break it; Solís is destroyed by transparency rather than violence; Sable's arc completes as she accepts that she cannot undo what her hands have done but can choose what they do next; the ending is neither triumphant nor tragic but earned — a woman who was a tool becoming the inoculation against the people who made her one.
